$comment: Cat Metro - RevenueCat entitlement + consumable contract. v1, 2026-07-31. Locked against DECISIONS_BRIEF.md and specs/revenuecat_implementation.md (entitlement attach, offering IDs) and specs/monetization_spec.md (runtime effects, suppression, revocation). Machine-readable companion to revenuecat_configuration.csv.

app.identity_model: anonymous RevenueCat App User IDs only - no accounts, no Purchases.LogIn; the only identity link is the $onesignalUserId subscriber attribute

global_rules.single_check_principle: Game code checks exactly ONE entitlement id per feature. Umbrella products (cm_all_access, cm_supporter_pack) are attached directly to the theme entitlements in the RevenueCat dashboard so no boolean algebra ever appears in client code.
global_rules.grant_choke_point: Only EntitlementCache.ApplyCustomerInfo (non-consumables) and ConsumableLedger.TryGrant (consumables) may mutate durable ownership state. Both run on the main thread and commit through one atomic save write (temp+rename).
global_rules.source_of_truth: RevenueCat CustomerInfo. The on-device cache is a projection, never an authority: it may only ADD certainty offline, never invent or expire ownership.
global_rules.revocation_authority: An entitlement is revoked if and only if a fresh CustomerInfo says so. Offline, clock changes, cache staleness, reinstall, and save-file migration may NEVER revoke anything.
global_rules.payer_suppression: Any active all_access or supporter entitlement suppresses every system-initiated commerce surface (post_level_5, district-complete shop card, bonus_district lock, theme upsells, All Access cross-lines). Enforced in one place: OfferEligibilityService. QA hard gate: zero paywall_viewed events for suppressed surfaces on a payer.

granted_by.note: The primary purchase. Sold at post_level_5, bonus_district and shop.
Attached to all_access as well as supporter so a Supporter buyer never has to also buy All Access.

Experiment-only SKU (PW01, $6.99 vs $4.99). Play prices are per-SKU so the cheap arm needs its own product. Created Aug 1, INACTIVE at launch, attached to all_access + theme_sakura + theme_neon BEFORE it is ever activated, deactivated at experiment end.

runtime_effects.detail: Night Harbor district (10 handcrafted levels) becomes playable; the map tile stops rendering the All Access label and the lock view is never presented again.
Sakura Line and Neon Line become owned. Implemented via the RC dashboard attach (this product also activates theme_sakura and theme_neon) - NOT via client-side inference.
runtime_effects.code_hook: ThemeWardrobe binds to theme_sakura / theme_neon entitlement ids only

runtime_effects.detail: Daily free rewind goes from 1/day to 2/day. Applied at local-midnight refill; a mid-day grant tops the day up to 2 rather than adding 2.

Contractual: Cat Metro ships zero forced ad surfaces at 1.0, so this promise removes nothing today. It binds every future build - if any interstitial/banner/app-open surface is ever added post-launch, all_access holders are excluded permanently. Rewarded, player-initiated ads remain available to All Access owners because the player asks for them.
Gold badge renders on the profile header and the level results screen.

post_level_5 never fires (even if unfired), district-complete shop card never renders, bonus_district lock view is unreachable, theme rows render Owned, All Access cross-lines are stripped from ofr_themes and ofr_rewind renders. Still shown: rewind packs (the only honest offer to a payer) and the reframed Supporter card in shop.

offline_behavior.served_from: EntitlementCache snapshot persisted inside the main save file (atomic temp+rename write)
offline_behavior.answer_latency: synchronous from disk at boot; the game never shows a spinner to answer an ownership question
offline_behavior.expiry: none - non-consumable entitlements are honored indefinitely offline
offline_behavior.staleness: IsStale at >30 days since last successful CustomerInfo fetch. Staleness raises reconcile priority and logs error_caught(domain=entitlement_cache_stale). It NEVER downgrades, gates, or nags.
offline_behavior.reconcile: Background GetCustomerInfo at boot and on every foreground; on error the cache is kept untouched and the fetch is retried next foreground.
offline_behavior.clock_tamper: Device clock changes cannot revoke: revocation requires an explicit RC answer, not a time comparison.

revocation_behavior.detected_via: CustomerInfo delta -> EntitlementCache.ApplyCustomerInfo emits entitlement_changed(entitlement_id=all_access, change=revoked, source=refund)
revocation_behavior.applied_when: next session boundary or next Home visit - NEVER mid-level (hard gate; a level in progress always finishes)
content_effects: Night Harbor relocks but retains every star, score and completion record - repurchase resumes exactly where the player left off
Equipped premium theme reverts to the default cream/navy/teal/orange board at the next Home load, silently
Daily free rewind returns to 1/day at the next local-midnight refill; already-granted rewinds are not clawed back
Gold conductor badge is removed with no ceremony and no message
revocation_behavior.commerce_effects: All system-initiated paywalls suppressed for 30 days (post_level_5 stays once-ever and does not re-arm). Player-initiated surfaces (shop, bonus_district on tap, theme_preview on tap) remain available and are styled normally - no urgency, no discount, no win-back offer.
revocation_behavior.messaging: One quiet IAM: 'Your refund was processed. Your Night Harbor progress is saved if you ever come back.' CTA: OK. No shaming, no counter-offer.
revocation_behavior.downstream: payer_status user property downgraded; OneSignal tag updated via the RC integration so the account exits payer journeys and re-enters the ordinary lifecycle after the 30-day window.

qa: Buy cm_all_access on a clean license-tester account -> all_access + theme_sakura + theme_neon active in one CustomerInfo
Airplane-mode cold start with a cached grant -> bonus district playable, zero network spinner, boot log entitlements=cache
Device clock +31 days offline -> still owned; only error_caught(domain=entitlement_cache_stale) logged
Refund with revoke -> three entitlement_changed(revoked) events, relock at a session boundary, stars intact

The same product also activates all_access, so every All Access runtime effect applies. The shop card discloses this overlap explicitly rather than selling it twice.
runtime_effects.code_hook: none - handled entirely by the RC dashboard product attach

offline_behavior.note: The name-a-cat cameo string lives in the save and works offline forever, including during a CustomerInfo outage.

revocation_behavior.detected_via: entitlement_changed(entitlement_id=supporter, change=revoked) plus the same event for all_access, theme_sakura and theme_neon (one product, four entitlements)
content_effects: Founder livery unequips to the default livery at the next Home load
The typed cat name is retained in the save but stops rendering on the board; it returns intact if the pack is ever repurchased
All all_access revocation effects apply simultaneously
revocation_behavior.commerce_effects: Same 30-day system-paywall suppression as all_access. The Supporter card itself remains visible in the shop with its normal honesty line - a refund is not a reason to hide the product, only a reason to stop pushing it.

Buy cm_all_access -> supporter NOT active (negative test)
Refund cm_supporter_pack -> four revoked events; typed cat name still present in the save file after revocation

offline_behavior.equipped_state: The equipped theme id is a separate save field, so an owned theme stays equipped across offline sessions, reinstalls (after Restore) and CustomerInfo outages.
offline_behavior.rental_interaction: A rewarded theme_rental (3 levels, 1/theme/day) is a LOCAL timer, not an entitlement. If connectivity drops mid-rental the remaining levels are still honored - the rental counts levels, not clock time or network calls.

consumables.policy: Rewind packs deliberately carry NO RevenueCat entitlement. Rewinds are spent, not owned, so ownership semantics would be wrong and would break restore expectations. Fulfillment is a local, durable, append-only ledger; RevenueCat webhooks are an independent audit trail, never a grant path.

products.per_unit_claim: $0.25/rewind vs $0.40 in the 5-pack - the only comparative badge allowed, and it is arithmetically true

storage.location: inside the main save file - not a separate file, so it cannot drift from the balance it authorizes
storage.write_mode: atomic temp+rename via ISave.CommitAtomic(); the ledger entry, the dedupe hash and the rewind balance land in ONE durable write or none of them do
storage.audit_entries: List<Entry>{txnHash, productId, qty, grantedAtUtc} capped at the most recent 200 (FIFO trim)
storage.dedupe_set: HashSet<string> of granted txn hashes is NEVER trimmed - trimming it would re-open double-grant on redelivery. Bounded by lifetime consumable purchases per install (single digits in practice).

key.derivation: SHA-256 over the store transaction id, first 16 bytes rendered as 32 lowercase hex chars
key.privacy: The raw store transaction id never leaves the device and is never logged. Only the hash appears in analytics, as the taxonomy field txn_id_hash on purchase_completed.
key.collision_note: 128 bits of a SHA-256 digest keyed on store-unique transaction ids - collision risk is not a practical concern at any plausible scale.

grant_exactly_once.rule: TryGrant(transactionId, productId) is the ONLY function in the codebase that may increase the rewind balance from a purchase. There is no second grant site - the initial purchase callback and the redelivered-transaction path both funnel into it.
steps: 1. Look up the product in the quantity table {cm_rewind_5:5, cm_rewind_20:20}; unknown product id -> return 0 (never guess a quantity)
3. If the hash is already in the dedupe set -> log error_caught(domain=ledger_dedupe, context=productId) and return 0. This is an EXPECTED path, not an error condition
4. Add the hash, append the audit entry, increment the balance, CommitAtomic - one write
5. Emit purchase_completed(product_id, txn_id_hash) after the write succeeds, never before
grant_exactly_once.threading: Must be called on the main thread; the RevenueCat adapter marshals every SDK callback through MainThread.Post before touching the ledger. Dev builds assert MainThread.IsMainThread at the entry point and a violation is build-blocking.
grant_exactly_once.ordering_guarantee: The grant IS the write. Analytics is emitted after the durable write, so a crash between them costs an event (replayed from the queue) but never a grant.

process_death_safety.breadcrumb: purchase_breadcrumb{placementId, productId, state, startedAtUtc} is written on entering Purchasing and cleared at Done/Cancelled/Failed.
on_boot: Breadcrumb present -> enter Verifying silently; fetch CustomerInfo, or serve the cache and queue the fetch when offline
Consumables: RevenueCat redelivers unconsumed transactions on the next sync and each one is routed to TryGrant, where the dedupe set makes replay harmless
Breadcrumb expires after 72h with purchase_failed(error_domain=recovery, error_code=breadcrumb_expired); Play's own refund path protects the player if money actually moved
kill_scenarios_covered: Kill during the Play sheet -> purchase completes on relaunch through redelivery, or cleanly voids; never a stuck modal
Kill immediately after the success toast, before any further save -> the atomic commit already held the grant; relaunch shows the balance and one ledger row
Three consecutive relaunches with a redelivered transaction -> balance moves exactly once, two dedupe logs
process_death_safety.pending_purchases: Billing pending/deferred purchases are a first-class state, not an error. UI: 'Your payment is processing. We'll deliver automatically as soon as Google Play confirms - keep playing!' Completion may arrive in a later session and still lands exactly once.

webhook_reconciliation.endpoint: https://rc-hooks.catmetro.io/v1/revenuecat (Cloudflare Worker, append-only KV log, Authorization-header shared secret)
webhook_reconciliation.primary_event: NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE - this is the consumable fulfillment signal for cm_rewind_5 / cm_rewind_20
webhook_reconciliation.job: Nightly cron compares NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE counts per product against device-reported purchase_completed(txn_id_hash) rows; any mismatch emails a one-line alert with the hashed ids
webhook_reconciliation.non_authority: The webhook NEVER grants, never revokes and is never in the purchase path. The game does not know the endpoint exists and never blocks on it. Its only jobs are dispute evidence, refund visibility and a 7-day zero-mismatch gate before the production submit.
webhook_reconciliation.gate: 7 consecutive days of zero mismatches during the commercial beta is a release-readiness item

spend_and_sources.balance: One integer in the save. Purchased, free-daily and rewarded rewinds all land in it; the SOURCE is recorded per use via rewind_used(source=free|purchased|rewarded, balance_after).
spend_and_sources.spend_order: today's free rewind -> owned balance -> rewarded ad -> purchase. Purchase rows always render below the free options (brief-locked: purchase secondary).
spend_and_sources.offline: Rewinds are fully usable offline: spending decrements the local balance and queues the analytics event. Only ACQUIRING a pack needs the network.
spend_and_sources.eligibility_floor: The rewind sheet cannot even be fetched on attempt 1 of any level - a hard EditMode-tested rule, not a UI convention.
spend_and_sources.never_required: Every level is solver-validated as completable with zero rewinds; the sheet footer states this and it is true.

refund_behavior.consumed_rewinds: NOT clawed back on a rewind-pack refund - goodwill, and clawing back a spent convenience would corrupt a live save for pennies
refund_behavior.ledger_annotation: The refunded transaction hash is annotated from the CANCELLATION webhook so repeat refund-farming is visible
refund_behavior.abuse_response: >2 refunded consumable purchases on an account -> pack rows hidden for that account; free, daily and rewarded rows are unaffected (the game stays fully playable and fair)
refund_behavior.no_entitlement_impact: A rewind refund changes no entitlement and triggers no revocation path - the two systems are deliberately disjoint

restore_semantics.rule: Consumables are NOT restorable. Restore copy must never imply otherwise.
restore_semantics.copy: An account whose only history is rewind packs sees 'No purchases found on this Google account.' plus the account-switch hint - never a false-hope 'restoring your rewinds' message.

cross_references.monetization_spec: deliverables/specs/monetization_spec.md (sections 3.11-3.14: suppression, failed purchase, restore, refund)
